headline: Anthropic starts trading on Nasdaq today while crypto platforms sell tokens that track its shares; bitcoin is near $64,000 but heading for a seventh straight weekly loss as Fed rate-rise fears weigh.

stories.title: Anthropic starts trading on Nasdaq today, and crypto platforms sell tokens that track its shares
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic sold shares at $83, above its $70-78 range, and starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday. Counting a private placement, it raised about $107 billion, more than SpaceX's IPO. Crypto platforms are selling tokens that track the share price. These tokens are not shares, and many are not open to US residents.
points: Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83, raising about $81.3 billion, or about $107.3 billion including a $26 billion private placement, at a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, per Al Jazeera.
CoinDesk says the total beats SpaceX's $86 billion, and that gray-market trading pointed to an opening as much as 24% higher than the offer price.
The first trade can come hours after the 9:30am ET open: SpaceX's came at 11:46am, per Stocktitan.
Kraken's page says its tokenized IPO access is not open to US clients, who can buy ANT as a regular stock from its first trading day.

CZ says tokenized versions on BNB Chain go live on IPO day, per CoinDesk; Binance Wallet's tokens are issued by Backed, are not Anthropic stock and carry no voting or dividend rights, per Bitcoin.com.

stories.title: Bitcoin climbs back toward $64,000 but heads for a seventh straight weekly loss
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell close to $62,000 overnight, then climbed back toward $64,000 early Thursday as tech stocks rose ahead of Anthropic's debut. It is still on track for a seventh weekly loss in a row. Worries about further Fed rate rises and heavy November outflows from US bitcoin funds keep pressure on.
points: CoinDesk says bitcoin is heading for its seventh straight weekly loss, its second-longest losing run after nine weeks in 2022, having fallen from about $87,500 to $62,000.
Minutes of the Fed's last meeting showed some officials were ready to raise rates by more than the usual quarter point, per CoinDesk.
US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $306.5 million on Wednesday 18 Nov, with none of the 12 funds taking in money, and November outflows are near $2.9 billion, per Coinpaper.
Global stablecoin supply fell about $16 billion in 30 days to $286 billion, per Nansen data reported by crypto.news.

stories.title: Ledger finds tampered hardware wallets sold in Berlin and Dubai
stories.summary: Ledger widened its investigation into tampered hardware wallets to Berlin and Dubai. Attackers obtained real devices, physically modified them to capture the recovery phrase during setup, and put them back into reseller channels. Ledger says there is no flaw in its chip or operating system and no confirmed case involving a device bought directly from Ledger.com. It asks anyone who bought a device in Berlin since January to contact support.
points: Tampered units were reported in Dubai and a small number in Berlin, per Cryptowisser.
Two users report about $604,000 lost combined from devices bought from an authorized Dubai reseller; Ledger has yet to confirm the total, per Cryptowisser.
Bitquery estimates about $1.68 million taken from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, after about $102 million from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia earlier, per Cryptowisser.
Ledger says there is no flaw in its secure chip or operating system and no confirmed case involving a device bought directly from Ledger.com, per Cryptowisser.

sources.label: Cryptowisser: $1.68M traced to Berlin and Dubai

briefs.title: Binance wins $6.5B freezing order over October hack
briefs.summary: An Abu Dhabi court granted a worldwide freezing order; Binance says about $2.85 billion of about $6.34 billion in affected assets has been frozen or intercepted, per The Block.

briefs.title: Senators ask Treasury to treat state stablecoin issuers equally
briefs.summary: Senators including Lummis and Gillibrand asked Treasury Secretary Bessent to give state-regulated stablecoin issuers the same safe harbor as federal ones under the GENIUS Act, per KuCoin News.

briefs.title: Movie2K defendant offered deal to hand over 40,000 BTC
briefs.summary: A Leipzig judge offered to drop the case if the defendant gives up 40,000 bitcoin plus €38 million; the trial resumes 3 Dec, per Decrypt.

briefs.title: Coinbase blocks $4.7M headed to a deepfake giveaway
briefs.summary: Coinbase's AI defenses stopped about $4.7 million going to scammers running a fake Elon Musk giveaway livestream, per The Block.

briefs.title: World Bank tests USDC payouts
briefs.summary: The World Bank Group is testing USDC with Circle and Citi for disbursements, per The Block.

briefs.title: Variational raises $110M
briefs.summary: The onchain derivatives platform raised a $110 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, led by Bain Capital Crypto, per The Block.

briefs.title: Russia lists 30 licensed crypto operators
briefs.summary: Russia's central bank register lists 30 operators including Sberbank and VTB, with a 300,000-ruble yearly cap for retail buyers, per BitcoinWorld.

calendar.event: US jobless claims and Philly Fed survey
calendar.note: Claims forecast 197,000, prior 200,000, per TD Economics. Philly Fed prior 20.9, per Trading Economics; no consensus could be confirmed. Walmart reports at 7:00am ET, per Finviz. Fed's Hammack speaks at 8:50am ET, per TD Economics, and Vice Chair Jefferson at 9:25am ET, per the Fed.

calendar.event: Anthropic's first day of trading on Nasdaq as ANT
calendar.note: Priced at $83, per Al Jazeera. The market opens at 9:30am ET, but a new listing's first trade comes in Nasdaq's IPO Cross, which can be hours after the open (SpaceX's came at 11:46am), per Stocktitan.

SEC nominees Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine appear before the Senate Banking Committee with other nominees, per the committee's page. Fed's Goolsbee (12:30pm ET), Barkin (4:00pm ET) and Paulson (6:30pm ET) speak, per TD Economics, and Barr at 2:15pm ET, per the Fed.

calendar.event: Token unlocks: KAITO, ZRO, ARIA, AKE, MBG, SOON, MON, SOSO, XPL, H, HUMA
calendar.note: Unlock dates are UTC. KAITO and ZRO on Friday 20, ARIA and AKE on Saturday 21, MBG on Sunday 22, SOON on Monday 23, MON (the largest, about $247M) and SOSO on Tuesday 24, XPL and H on Wednesday 25, HUMA on Thursday 26 November. KAITO's 00:00 UTC unlock is 7:00pm ET Thursday. See the unlock table on this page for sizes, dates and confidence. (Dates from this desk's unlock data.)

Deribit options settle at 08:00 UTC, per Deribit. Cryptoticker puts Friday's bitcoin expiry at about 28,300 BTC, roughly $1.8 billion. The bigger monthly expiry, about $5.7 billion per Cryptoticker, is Fri 27 Nov.

calendar.event: University of Michigan consumer sentiment (Nov, final)
calendar.note: Forecast 51.0 and preliminary November reading 51.0, per FinanceCalendar. October's final reading is 48.0 per FinanceCalendar but 46.3 per InvestingLive. Fed's Waller speaks at 8:25am ET and Cook at 12:15pm ET (00:15 Sat Bangkok), per the Fed.
Prior 91.7, per WDBJ7 (AP); no forecast found. Dell, Workday and HP report after the US close, per IfYouSpent.

calendar.event: US GDP (Q3 second estimate), PCE inflation (Oct), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: BEA confirms Q3 GDP (second estimate) and October personal income and PCE at 8:30am ET. Core PCE prior 3.1% a year, per ForexFundamentals. Durable goods forecast +0.2%, per Continuum Economics. Weekly jobless claims move to Wednesday for Thanksgiving, per FinanceCalendar. Fed Beige Book at 2:00pm ET, per the Fed.

calendar.event: Thanksgiving: US stock market closed, then early close
calendar.note: NYSE closed Thursday and closes at 1:00pm ET Friday, per ICE. The monthly bitcoin options expiry is Friday at 08:00 UTC (15:00 Bangkok), about $5.7 billion per Cryptoticker.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Meeting 8-9 Dec, statement 2:00pm ET and press conference 2:30pm ET Wed 9 Dec (02:30 Thu Bangkok), per the Fed. CME FedWatch prices about a 95% chance of a December rate rise, per 24/7 Wall St.
